name: TX-14
label: Likely R

Weber's large financial advantage ($972K raised vs $27K, Bartie in the red)

model.rationale: Randy Weber holds a seat that leans twelve points Republican, has out-raised Thurman Bartie by roughly 36-to-1, and faces an opponent with negative cash on hand. Markets price his win probability around 95%, and no polling or ratings suggest movement toward the Democrat.
model.watch: A surprise wave-level Democratic environment in Texas could tighten the race, but Bartie's minimal fundraising leaves little room for that to matter.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Randy Weber seeks another term in a Southeast Texas district that voted twelve points Republican at the presidential level in recent cycles. He enters the general election with a well-funded campaign, nearly $922,000 in cash, and no outside groups spending against him. Thurman Bartie, the Democratic nominee, has raised only about $27,000 and reports negative cash on hand, leaving him little capacity to communicate with voters.

Prediction markets give Weber roughly a 95% chance of returning to office, and no public polls or expert ratings point to a competitive race. The fundamentals — district lean, incumbency, and the money gap — all favor the incumbent, making this a safe seat for Republicans barring an unforeseen shift in the national environment.
